desc:
Cards lie in a row, and cards[i] is the number printed on the i-th card. You want to pick up a block of consecutive cards that contains two cards with the same number.

Return the smallest number of cards in such a block, or -1 if no two cards share a number.

cards = [3, 4, 2, 3, 4, 7]
block [3, 4, 2, 3] has two 3s and holds 4 cards
result = 4
hints: A block contains a repeated number exactly when it contains two equal cards. Which pair of equal cards makes the block as short as possible?
For one number, only neighbouring occurrences matter: a block through two occurrences with another occurrence between them could be shortened.
Scan left to right and remember the last index where each number was seen. At index i with a previous index j, the block [j, i] has i - j + 1 cards.
editorial: The best block always starts and ends on two equal cards that are consecutive occurrences of the same number; any other block with a duplicate can be trimmed down to such a pair. So the answer is the smallest distance between two consecutive occurrences of the same value, plus one.

Keep a hash map from value to the last index where it appeared. When the current card already has an entry, update the answer with i - last + 1, then store the new index. This is the same as a sliding window whose left edge jumps to the previous occurrence. One pass gives O(n) time and O(n) space. Checking every block directly would be O(n2) or worse.
